AlternateTargets: the eye at the top of the head
Senses.Note: The corpus gives no anatomical account beyond the crown-of-the-head image. Common extensions are “possess the crown-gate eye” (54 hits in 29 files), “open the crown-gate eye” (19/16), “throw open the crown-gate eye” (9/8), and “the correct eye at the crown-gate” (142/85). The longer “one eye at the crown-gate” appears twice. These are recorded as morphology and deployment, not recast as an imported concept.

SearchAliases: the eye at the crown of the head
the eye at the top of the head
Senses.Explanation: The phrase pictures an extra eye at the crown of the head; speakers require, open, test, or attribute this eye in public encounters. The records use it with the verbs possess, open, look, illuminate, and strike blind, and with the adjective correct. Lushan Fazhen says that to understand the upward matter one must possess the crown-gate eye; possessing it accords with the heart of leaving home, and he then asks, “do you want to understand the crown-gate eye?” before saying that people in the four capitals put on clothes and eat while people in the two Zhejiang circuits are full and warm (欲明向上事，須具頂門眼；要會頂門眼麼？四京人著衣喫飯，兩浙人飽暖自如). Yuanwu invites “those who possess the crown-gate eye” to raise Xuansha's case (具頂門眼者，請試舉看), and says in verse that when the crown-gate eye is correct it has complete efficacy (頂門眼正有全功). Dahui says a flash of lightning opens the crown-gate eye (激電爍開頂門眼). In a direct exchange, the cited participant says the furnace has opened it; Chaozong Tongren asks what it is, the cited participant bows, and Chaozong Tongren strikes him and says, “it has been knocked blind” (擉瞎了也). A transmission record appraises Zhaozhou as possessing it while distinguishing black and white in a stone-struck spark (趙州具頂門眼，向擊石火裏分緇素). The term occurs 276 times in 123 allowlisted files. Jifei Ruyi directly turns the image back into a public question, asking, “What is the eye at the crown?” This questioning use concerns the same eye-image, not another object.
